title: Miri Standard SDK Manifest
description: Schema for sdk-manifest.json - Core API index with structured signatures and metadata

sdk_version.description: Version of the SDK package (PEP 440); accepts epoch, multi-segment release, pre/post/dev, and local versions so it never rejects a valid wheel version

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when metadata was generated

primary_classes.description: Main classes agents should know about

key_methods.description: Most important methods across all classes

common_imports.description: Standard import statements for the SDK

code_index.description: Where a precomputed code index lives in this wheel and what format it is in, so a consumer can DISCOVER it and decide whether it can read it before opening it. Optional, and MIRI-PY-045 is a SHOULD: no toolchain produces these for wheels yet. The standard names the format and not the producer, exactly as it names the wheel format and not the build backend. Declaring the format is the load-bearing part - a protobuf index is far cheaper than the source when queried for one symbol and more expensive than the source when read whole, so a consumer that cannot decode it needs to know that from the manifest rather than from a failed parse, and fall back to `api_index`.

path.description: Path within the wheel, under `.dist-info/` beside the SBOM documents PEP 770 places there — one convention for precomputed artifacts rather than two. MUST be listed in RECORD like every other carried file.

format.description: A closed set of one. SCIP is a published format with a protobuf schema, several indexers and existing consumers; the standard adopting it rather than maintaining its own graph is the whole point of withdrawing api-graph.json. Adding a format here is a schema change, deliberately, so two wheels never describe the same thing differently.

reduction.description: Which sections were removed before shipping. A full index measured 62% of a 1.87 MB wheel against 20% with reference occurrences removed, so shipping one unreduced is usually wrong — but WHICH reduction is safe is unsettled: if third-party readers locate definitions through definition occurrences rather than through SymbolInformation, stripping all occurrences breaks them. Declared so a consumer knows what it was handed instead of inferring it, and so the answer can be measured across implementations before the standard prescribes one.

produced_by.description: Indexer name and version, informative. Recorded because two producers emitting different symbol IDs for the same code would break cross-release deltas, and that has not been tested across two indexers.

api_index.description: Index of the public API components a consumer can route to. Keys are dotted qualified names, in the key space the Discovery Contract's `resolve` (§3.6) and `graph` (§3.5) operations address: `Greeter`, `api.tenants.list_tenants`. A method is addressed as `Greeter.greet` and RESOLVED by walking into the class entry's `key_methods`, so it is not a key of that spelling here. Before 0.8.0 this pattern admitted only a bare identifier, which contradicted that contract, and because `additionalProperties` was unset a dotted key was validated against nothing at all rather than refused. A `module`-typed entry carries its public members under `members`, so a name defined in many modules keeps one entry per module instead of one entry in total. This is a ROUTING map and not an inventory of every public definition: console-script entry points MUST be excluded (Agent Metadata §5.4), and a producer MAY describe a narrower surface by declaring `surface_coverage`. Membership here never settles whether a symbol exists, which is what `resolve` is for (MIRI-CONSUMER-010).

surface_coverage.description: Whether `api_index` describes the whole importable surface or a producer-declared subset of it. Defaults to "complete" when omitted, so every manifest written before 0.8.0 keeps its meaning. "declared" states that the producer scoped the walk, and REQUIRES `surface_scope`, so a consumer reading an absent symbol can tell "not in this package" from "not in the declared scope". This distinction is also what lets a linter tell an empty delta from a delta it could not measure: against a complete surface an empty delta is an exclusion, and against a declared one it is a forfeit (MIRI-PY-043). Modelled on `advisory_coverage` in cli-describe-v1.json, which defaults to the strong claim and couples the weak one to the field that makes it actionable.

exclude.description: The patterns excluded from `api_index`, relative to the installed package directory, POSIX-spelled. MATCHING IS fnmatch, not pathlib: a `*` CROSSES directory separators, so `api/*` and `api/**` both match `api/a/b.py`. The dialect is stated because two implementations diverge here silently otherwise, and because `PurePath.full_match`, the obvious alternative, arrived in Python 3.13 and is unavailable to a producer supporting 3.11. NEGATION IS NOT SUPPORTED, and neither is directory-only matching: a pattern never re-includes what an earlier one excluded, so the order of this array carries no meaning. Should negation be added, it will be specified as last-match-wins at the same time, since an unstated precedence is where implementations disagree without noticing.

surface_scope.description: What a declared surface left out. Required when `surface_coverage` is "declared" and meaningless otherwise, because a complete surface excluded nothing.

environment_variables.description: Environment variables used by the SDK

type.description: The kind of component. A METHOD is not among them, deliberately: a method appears under its class's `key_methods`, which is where `MIRI-PY-031` already resolves one ("a class, a method under `key_methods`, or a module-level function"). A draft of 0.8.0 added `method` here so that a top-level `Greeter.greet` entry would validate, which an attack fixture happened to need; it was removed before release because a test needing a shape is a weaker reason to bless it than a producer needing it, and two conforming documents for one package is a cost every consumer pays forever. Raised by the miri-py team, whose generator has never emitted a top-level method key. `api-graph-v1.json` keeps `method` among its NODE kinds, which is a different vocabulary: a graph addresses what exists, while this index routes to where it is described.

members.description: The public members of a `module`-typed entry, keyed by bare name. Added at 0.8.0 so that a name defined in many modules keeps one entry per module rather than one entry in total: a generated client whose 431 endpoint modules each define `sync` previously kept one. A consumer walks this the way MIRI-PY-031 already walks `key_methods`, so bare-name lookup is unaffected and no existing consumer migrates.

signature.description: The component's call signature as it appears in source, e.g. "Greeter(language: str = 'en')". An AST fact. Optional: a generator emits it where the source states it, and a consumer MUST NOT assume its presence (Discovery Contract §3.5).

raises.description: Exception types that may be raised
